After compounding cumulative price increases exceeding 30% between 2022 and 2024, the franchise hit an acute consumer elasticity wall across its flagship, highest-margin engine, Frito-Lay North America (PFNA). Wall Street remains skeptical of management's turnaround execution, noting that aggressive price rollbacks of up to 15% across key snack lines and a 20% domestic SKU rationalization have delivered flat volume response while diluting segment margins.

Furthermore, institutional bears see secular impairment rather than routine cyclical softness. A heavily levered balance sheet with $53.2B in debt (-$31.34 net cash per share), persistent channel foot-traffic declines in high-margin convenience and gas stations, and accelerating health headwinds from GLP-1 adoption and ultra-processed food scrutiny have caused the market to re-rate PepsiCo as a mature, capital-intensive packaged goods operator facing terminal multiple compression rather than an elite compounder.
